# Atal Bihari VajpayeeIndian Institute of Information Technology & Management, Gwalior (An Institute ofNational Importance under Ministry of HRD,Government of India) 

## **Ref:  ABVIIITMG/2026/325** 

**Date: 5**<sup>**th**</sup> **June, 2026** 

## **<u>Advertisement for the JRF Position in the ANRF Sponsored Project</u>** 

Applications are invited from eligible candidates as a Junior Research Fellow (JRF) to work on the following project sponsored by ANRF under the supervision of Dr. Rahul Kala, **ABV-IIITM, Gwalior** . The duration of the position extends for a maximum of three years, extendable upto five years, or the duration of the project, whichever is earlier. The candidates can be enrolled in the Ph.D. program as per the institute norms. The project is being done in collaboration with NIT Mizoram. 

The details related to the project are as follows:

metadata.section: Atal Bihari VajpayeeIndian Institute of Information Technology & Management, Gwalior (An Institute ofNational Importance under Ministry of HRD,Government of India)

text:
|**Project No. and Title**|ANRF/ARG/2025/009728/ENS Socially-Interactive Vacuum Cleaning Robot for On-Human Demand
and Human-Instructed Cleaning| |---|---|

metadata.section: Advertisement for the JRF Position in the ANRF Sponsored Project

text:
|---|---| |**About the Project**|Robotic vacuum cleaners are on a steep rise in India. The Indian market has two unique problems that
pose a severe limitation: Target cleaning of room segments, certain surfaces, and only some dirty areas to
be cleaned on demand; and perceiving humans, anticipating their motion, guessing their intents and
behaviours, and thus take a path that is socially compliant during daytime cleaning. The project aims to
design a system that allows a human to call the robot; allow the human to instruct the robot about the
cleaning task via speech and hand gestures; perform a semantic understanding of the robot map and the
current perception; make the robot socially compliant with humans; allow following the person for
segments of the journey, enabling the human to point to the area or allowing the human to inspect the
cleaning and give further instructions if needed.| |**Principal Investigator(PI)**|Dr. Rahul Kala|

metadata.section: Advertisement for the JRF Position in the ANRF Sponsored Project

text:
|**Principal Investigator(PI)**|Dr. Rahul Kala| |**Fellowship**|As per the DST norms.| |**Essential**
**Qualifications**|Candidates must have M.Tech/ M.S./M.E. or equivalent in CSE (Computer Science and Engineering) / IT
(Information Technology) / EC (Electronics and Communication)/ Electrical Engineering/ degrees or
equivalent. They must also have B. Tech/ B.E./M.Sc. in CSE/IT/EC/EE or equivalent.
Candidates must also have qualified GATE/NET in the relevant area for the JRF position.
In the absence of GATE/NET,**Project Associate**position may be considered, with monthly emoluments
in accordance with DST norms.| |**Desirable Qualification:**|Basics of machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, robotics or large language models| |**Application Deadline**|6thJuly, 2026|

text:
**Application Procedure:** 

- Candidates are requested to send their detailed CV, including their academic details with percentage/CGPA, research works/projects, and work experience (if any) to <u>rkala@iiitm.ac.in</u> with the subject line as “Application for the JRF position in the DST sponsored project.”

Criteria for Earnest Money Deposit (E.M.D): 

a)           It is pertinent to mention that the benefit of EMD exemption and purchase preference under MSM E shall be applicable only to **manufacturers of the respective goods** . Any trader, including an authoriz ed dealer of the OEM, submitting an MSME certificate shall not be considered under the MSME category for this bid, and the benefit of EMD exemption shall not be applicable to such firms. Micro and Small Enterpris es (MSEs) must hold a valid Udyam Registration, and their credentials shall be verified through the Udyam portal and supporting documents by the Institute.

link was for 10 years (commissioned in 2010). The Institute has a 30 Mbps (1:1) alternate internet
leased line from Railtel. Whenever the internet connectivity from BSNL goes down the entire load
of the institute comes on 3o Mbps internet line from Railtel then there are frequent complaints
from students regarding poor bandwidth and disruption of normal academic activities of the
students.

### **<u>Advertisement for the JRF/Project Associate Position in the DST Sponsored Project</u>** 

Applications are invited from eligible candidates as a Junior Research Fellow (JRF) or Project Associate-1 to work on the following project sponsored by DST under the supervision of Dr. Rahul Kala, **ABV-IIITM, Gwalior** . There is only one position available. The selections would be made for the JRF position. If no candidate is found suitable for the JRF position, candidates for the Project Associate position would be considered. The duration of the position extends upto the duration of the project (about 1.5 years). The candidates can be enrolled in the Ph.D. program as per the institute norms. The project is being done in collaboration with the University of Wisconsin—Madison, IIT Jammu and IIIT Allahabad. The candidate is expected to have active and engaging discussions between all the project partners. The details related to the project are as follows:

metadata.section: Advertisement for the JRF/Project Associate Position in the DST Sponsored Project

text:
|**Project Title**|DST-NSF Turning “Tragedy of the Commons ToC” into “Emergent Cooperative Behavior ECB” for Automated
Vehicles at Intersections with Meta-Learning| |---|---| |**About the Project**|The objectives of this proposal include (1) understanding the fundamental automated vehicle (AV) ToC and human-
driven vehicle (HV) ECB phenomena at both structured US intersections and unstructured Indian Intersections with
drastically different settings, and (2) devising proper AV control to turn the AV ToC behavior into an ECB to support
more efficient traffic operations. A meta-learning-based AV control framework in a realistic decentralized setting will
be created to optimize mixed traffic intersection performance not only for local individual vehicles but also for overall
trafficperformance,which will be verified with both computer models andphysics tests.| |**Principal Investigator (PI)**|Dr. Rahul Kala| |**Fellowship**|As per the DST norms.|

Certificates for SC, ST, OBC, PH, EWS, etc., if relevant, should also be attached.

metadata.section: AtalBihariVajpayeeIndian Institute of Information Technology & Management, Gwalior (An InstituteofNationalImportanceunderMinistryofHRD,Governmentof India)

text: Applications are invited for the Junior Research Fellow (JRF) under the MPCST-funded research project titled “ **End-toEnd Deep Learning Model for Pulmonary Nodule Detection and Risk Characterization in Early Lung Cancer Screening** ” in the department of Computer Science and Engineering at ABV-Indian Institute of Information Technology and Management (ABV-IIITM) Gwalior. The appointment is purely temporary and will be governed by the terms and conditions of the funding agency and the Institute. The position is initially for ONE YEAR and may be extended further till the completion of the project based on satisfactory performance on reviewed conducted on every 06 months.

text:
|**Project Title**|**Development of AI/ML modules in ARISTO platform for chemotherapy automation**
**process**| |---|---| |**About the Project**|The proposed project aims to develop an end-to-end deep learning framework for automatic
pulmonary nodule detection and malignancy risk characterization from chest CT scans to
support early lung cancer screening. The system will integrate advanced deep learning
techniques for accurate nodule localization, feature extraction, and classification of nodules
as benign or malignant. By enabling reliable and early identification of suspicious nodules,
the project aims to improve lung cancer survival rates, reduce healthcare burden, and promote
accessible AI-assisted diagnostic solutions for large-scale screening programs.| |**PI & Co-PIs**|Prof. K. V. Arya (PI), Dr. Sunil Kumar (Co-PI), and Dr. Divya Gautam (Co-PI)|

##### **<u>Introduction</u>** 

ABV-Indian Institute of Information Technology and Management (ABV-IIITM) Gwalior is a premier educational institution declared as “Institute of National Importance” for Information Technology and Management education and research. The Institute is ful ly residential and all the bonafide students of the institute have to compulsorily opt f or hostel facility. There are 6 hostels in the campus, namely Aravali (BH-1), Nilgiri (B H-2), Shivalik (BH-3), Gangotri (GH), Srisailam (IVH), and Satpura. However, the mess facility will be run for 5 hostels, catering to the needs of all six hostels. Each hostel u sually houses students from all the years.

At present, in total all the hostels accommodate approximately 1571 students. A Student Welfare Society looks after the **5 messes** to provide meals to the resident s attached to each of these hostels. Each hostel has a “Mess Committee" of the resid ents and hostel administration, which is authorized to regulate the mess related acti vities on a day-to-day basis. The hostel’s administration includes a “Warden” and “As sistant Warden” nominated by the Institute for the operation of the mess contract an d other related welfare measures. Generally, the strength of the residents in each of the hostels (except IVH and Satpura hostel) remains around 325 students (±100 stu dents)) during the academic year. However, during the vacations, the strength of the students may reduce substantially. Every hostel has an adequate kitchen space, pip ed cooking gas, water supply, dining tables, etc.

35. The contract can be terminated by giving a one-month notice period by the ABV-IIITM Student Welfare Society  and three-month notice by the mess service provider. However, the authority reserves the right to terminate the contract without assigning any reason if it appears to the authority a

36. Coupons for guest meals and extra will be sold (given) to the customer either on the basis of a student writing for it in the register maintained for the purpose or against cash p ayment for the same to the mess service provider. The price of the same will be decided by Dean of Students Affairs in co nsultation with Council of Wardens.Furthermore,the institute may revise the guest charges at its discretion.

text:
37. No extra person from the outside of the institute other than institute faculty, staff and student’s guests are allowed in the mess area, any exception to this must have prior approval of Dean of Student Affairs /competent authority of the institute. 

38. The mess service provider and his workers must behave politely wit h the hostel inmates. The mess service provider shall enquire about the character of worker to be employed and ensure that there is no criminal case is pending or contemplated against that person. Then only, after sa tisfaction, mess service providershall depute/ deploy the person in hostel mess. The workers employed by mess service providershould be free fro m any contagious disease or sickness or any other kind of disease that is considered unacceptable for handling food. 

39. Food / any other item should not be served inside the room of hostel inmates except in exceptional cases or ill health on dire ctives of Warden only.

40. No accommodation will be provided in the campus for t he workers and the mess service provider shall make their own arrangements. 

41. Sufficient counters should be operational. The need will be decid ed by the Mess Committee. 

42. Catering services for institute events held within the premises of th e hostel may be undertaken only after obtaining a written permission fro m the mess council and warden at least three days prior to the event. 

43. In case the mess is closed on any occasion or for pest c ontrol then special dinner / lunch shall be provided, at no extra cost and the menu will be decided by mess committee 

44. Paper napkin should be provided when fried food is served. 

45. Filled salt and chat masala dispensers must be available on the t able at all times.

49. Mess service provider or his representative manager / supervisor is required to remain present in the mess when the food is cooked & serve d in the mess. The manager/supervisor must have a degree/diploma in h 

24 / 47 

otel management with relevant experience. It is the responsibility of the manager / supervisor to oversee all mess operations and especially ensu re that no lapses as stated above arise on day to day basis. One head ch ef must be deployed in each mess. 

50. The food quality will be paramount. If the mess manage ment is not up to the mark or the quality of the food is below standard or unhealthy or unhygienic, then the Dean of Stude nt Affairs (DoSA), on the recommendation of the respective Warden of Hostel Mess/Mess Committee, is empowered to te rminate the contract with a **short notice of one week** . Th e Hostel Mess Committee’s opinion is final as far as the food quality/mess management is concerned.

51. Upon termination of the mess service provider contract, on the reco mmendation of the warden and the mess committee, the DoSA has the a uthority to award the contract to any existing vendor to 

ensure uninterrupted mess services. 

52. The payment /calculation of the mess bill would be on the actual da ys of operation of the mess, and the actual number of students registere d. 

53. Liability/responsibility in case of an accident causing inj ury or illness/ death of mess worker(s) or any of his staff shal l be of the mess service provider. The Hostel Section / Institu te authority shall not be responsible by any means in such c ases.

54. The mess service provider shall be solely responsible in case of inci dence/s of food poisoning etc. and shall bear the complete expenditure a rising out of this for medical treatment of the hostel inmates. In addition, the penalty may be imposed on the mess service provider as decided by the Committee appointed by the Director/DoSA for such incidents. 

55. Storage/consumption of any alcoholic drink / liquor are strictly prohi bited. The mess service provider shall not serve any of such substances / drinks in mess / hostel. Smoking, consuming tobacco, pan masala etc. is also strictly prohibited in Institute premises. The mess service provider s hould also ascertain that his staff / workers are prohibited from storage / consumption of any alcoholic drink / liquor / drugs of any kind and ensure that they are not found in intoxicated condition any time either on camp us or outside.

The Ins titute reserves its right to release the payment only after it i s justified that mess service provider has fulfilled all liability and obligation.

58. Food inspection (both raw and cooked food) will be don e on regular basis by the Wardens/committee / team having expert appointed by the Institute authority.

On expiry/termination of the contract, all such property shall properly be handed over to the Institute in good & working condition. The institute would claim financial compensation for t he depreciation and damages as applicable from the mess service provid er. 

60. Theft / accident, fire, and other safety hazards, any type of loss/dam age of assets due to any such incident shall be the sole responsibility of t he mess service provider. The Institute shall in no way be liable for any s uch incident occurring during or in connection with the services.

Item 61.0 Openingremarks bytheChairpersonBoG

The Chairperson welcomed all the members in 61st (01/20-25) BoG meeting of the Institute and wished them a very happy and successful year 2025. He suggested that ABV-IITM Gwalior should actively work on application in the different sectors of Indian Industry and research organization such as DRDO, ISRO, etc. to utilize AI for their benefits and competitiveness. He appreciated the effortoftheInstitute in invitingDG (R&M)ofDRDO as chief guest andthe successful organization of 27th Foundation Day of the institute. Chairman also emphasized that efforts should be made to organize the Al awareness program and its application in different sector of the society.All the sudents along-with their faculty advisors should try to develop at least one Al application as part of their study at ABV-IIITM. For this, they can see and explore the syllabus and similar activities being carried out in the best Universities/College of the World like Harward, Stanford etc.

Later, since Quorum was present, he asked the Secretary BoG to take up agenda items for discussions and approvals. ###### 1.Preamble 

The primary goal of a Post-Doctoral Fellowship (PDF) Program is to develop professional and academic skills under the mentorship of an experienced researcher.The PDF Program at ABVIndian Instituteof Information Technology and Management, Gwalior(ABV-IIITM,Gwalior)aims to identify and motivate young researchers and provide them support for research in frontier areas of science, engineering, technology and management. There are two categories under this program, as given below:

metadata.section: Rules and Regulations for Post-Doctoral Fellowship (PDF)Program

text:
- 1.1. Institute Post-Doctoral Fellow (IPDF)-A Post-Doctoral Fellow admitted to the PDF Program of ABV-IIITM, Gwalior, through the procedures adopted by the Institute and avails fellowship from the Institute funds. The number of sanctioned IPDF positions is 02 per department * 05 departments = 10 per year, which can vary as per Institute policy from time to time. However, thenumberofPost-Doctoral Fellowsallottedtoany department in anyadmission cycledepends on the number of suitable candidates and mentors in the department, and unfilled seats of one department may be given to another department by the competent authority. 

- 1.2.External Funding based Post-DoctoralFellow(EFPDF)-APost-Doctoral Fellowadmitted to the PDF Program of ABV-IIITM, Gwalior, through the procedures adopted by the Institute and avails Fellowship from any recognized funding agencies like ANRE, CSIR, DST, etc.

- ABV-IIITM, Gwalior, provides an opportunity to young researchers as an Institute Post-Doctoral Fellow(IPDF)andExternal Funding-basedPost-DoctoralFellow(EFPDF). 

###### 2.Essential requirements forIPDF 

- 2.1. The applicant should be an Indian national with a PhD or equivalent doctorate degree (e.g., D.Sc.)awarded from a recognized Institute/University.The candidate must have secured at least a 6.5 CGPA on a 10-point scale grading system or 60% marks at the Bachelor's and Master's level from a recognized Technical Institute or University in a relevant discipline. CGPA/Percentage relaxation is allowed as per GOI norms. Candidates with a PhD Thesis submitted may also apply. However, the candidate must produce the certificate of award of a PhD Degree from their University/lnstitute before joining the PDF program.

- 2.2. At least one degree from graduation onward or work experience on a regular pay scale/guest faculty should be from CFTIs (preferably, IISc/IITs/IITs/NITs/IIMs/ISI/IISERs) or a foreign university with QS rank ≤500. 

- 2.3. The applicant should apply within 05 (five) years from the date of the award of a PhD degree (i.e., Defense date). 

- 2.4. The applicant, who has completed their PhD from ABV-IIITM, Gwalior, can apply for the IPDF program after O1 (one) year of completion of their PhD defense viva-voce approval date. 

- 2.5. Applicants must have at least 03 (three) publications in SCI/SSCI/SCIE indexed Q1 journals as perthelatest Journal CitationReport. 

- 2.6. There shall be a rolling advertisement for the PDF Program. The applicant should be at most 35 years of age at the time of submission of the application form. However, age relaxation is provided as per the norms of the Govt.of India.

- 2.7. Applicants working as regular employees in government/semi-government/PsU organizations 

PIcirgh 

must apply through proper channel or produce a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the employingorganizationatthetimeof presentation/interview. 

3. Selection criteria and process for appointing IPDF 

   - 3.1. The Institute level committee, constituted by the competent authority, will look into framing/amending the PDF Program guidelines, advertising, and preparing the department-wise seat allocation of the sanctioned seats with the approval of the competent authority. 

   - 3.2. The initial vacancy is 02 PDFs per department per year that can be modified from time to time asfaculty strength increases. 

   - 3.3. Applications from aspiring Post-Doctoral Fellows will be invited in a prescribed application form; the mentioned documents and a research proposal must support it at submission.

- 3.4. The research proposal submitted by the applicant must not be a mere extension of their PhD work. The expertise brought in by the applicant will be an important criterion in the selection process. Emphasis shall be given to the research proposal's novelty, outcome and implications. 

   - 3.5.Selection willbemade attheinstitutelevel. 

      - 3.5.1.The Institute Post-Doctoral Selection Committee (IPDSC) will scrutinize the preliminary scrutiny. 

      - 3.5.2. The shortlisted candidates must appear for the presentation/interview by a committee approved by the competent authority, ABV-IIITM, Gwalior. 

   - 3.6. The mentor will be decided by the competent authority in consultation with the HOD of the department concerned. 

###### 4.Period of engagement

###### 4.Period of engagement 

   - 4.1. The appointment of IPDF is purely a temporary and full-time assignment. The duration of the fellowship is 02 (two) years. However, the offer will initially be made for one year and is extendable to a maximum of up to two years based on performance evaluation. 

   - 4.2. A Progress Monitoring Committee (PMC) will evaluate the progress half-yearly based on quantifiable outcomes referencing the proposed deliverables and publications and recommend the extension accordingly. The extension of the fellowship shall be based on the recommendations ofthePMC. 

   - 4.3. The continuation of the IPDF depends on a satisfactory report of the PMC. The IPDF may be terminated prematurely if the report is unsatisfactory. 

   - 4.4. The duration of EFPDF will be as per the sponsoring agency's guidelines. 

- 5.Work assignments forIPDF

- 4.4. The duration of EFPDF will be as per the sponsoring agency's guidelines. 

- 5.Work assignments forIPDF 

   - 5.1. IPDF will be attached to the department and mentor(s) for carrying out full-time research in the approved area and other academic responsibilities, e.g., tutorial classes, laboratory work, conducting seminars and symposia. However, academic responsibilities must be at most 08 (eight) hours per week. 

   - 5.2. In addition to carrying out quality research work, the IPDF is expected to assist the mentor(s) in writing externally funded project proposals. 

   - 5.3. IPDFs shall be eligible to co-guide B. Tech./M. Tech. students in BTP and MTP along with their mentor withthe approval of the Dean of Academics Affairs on recommendations from the mentor, HOD and Dean of Research and Consultancy. 

Prirh 

   - 5.4.IPDF shall be required to submit a comprehensive progress report to the Dean of Research and Consultancy office at the end of each semester.

6. Targets to be achieved during the period of engagement 

   - 6.1. The Post-Doctoral Fellow must have a minimum of 01 (one) manuscript submitted in the SCI/SSCI/SCIE indexed Q1 journals in the 1st year along with the mentor. In the 2nd year, 01 (one) paper must be accepted in SCI/SSCI/SCIE indexed Q1 journals, and another paper must be submitted. 

   - 6.2. The Post-Doctoral Fellow will submit a half-yearly progress report to the PMC describing the research work carried out and research results, supported by reprints or proofs or manuscripts of the papers/patents published or accepted for publication for this purpose. 

   - 6.3. Further extension of the Post-Doctoral Fellow will be based on quantifiable outcomes and deliverables proposed in the initial proposal and the recommendations of the PMC. recommendationofthePMC.

- 6.5. The fellowship of a PDF may be terminated at any time if the research progress/conduct of the candidate is unsatisfactory by giving one month's notice to the PDF on the mentor's recommendation, forwarded through HOD and approved by the Dean of Research and Consultancy.Similarly,the PDF must give one month's notice through the mentor, forwarded through HOD and approved by the Dean of Research and Consultancy if they want to leave the fellowship before tenure completion. 

   - 6.6. The Institute will own any rights related to the Intellectual Property (IP) generated out of postdoctoral research and will be governed by the Institute's IPR policy, which may be amended from time to time. 

7. EligibilitytobementorforIPDF

7. EligibilitytobementorforIPDF 

- 7.1. The proposed mentor should have a PhD degree in the relevant discipline with at least 05 (five) years of post-PhD experience in Academia/Research & Development/Industry and be a regular faculty member (Pay level 12 and above in the 7th CPC) at the institute. 

- 7.2. The mentor(s) should work in the proposed/similar research area and have a proven record of SCI/SSCI/SCIEpublications.The mentor should have at least 10 (ten)publications in the abovementioned indexed journals. 

- 7.3. The mentor(s) should have supervised at least 02 (two) PhD students (awarded/thesis submitted) as a principal supervisor and another student awarded/submitted/under supervision. 

- 7.4. A mentor will be permitted to have up to 01 (one) fellow at any given time from the IPDF. The opportunity to take IPDF will rotate among the department faculties. If a Post-Doctoral Fellow works under the mentorship of more than O1 (one) mentor, the PDF shall be considered half.

- 7.5. If a Post-Doctoral Fellow leaves or is terminated, that vacancy will be carried forward. 

- 8.Fellowship and Leave rules 

   - 8.1. A fellowship of Rs. 60,000/- - 70,000/- per month (consolidated) will be offered as shown in Table 1 below, depending upon experience. This fellowship may be revised from time to time. Tablel:Fellowshipdependinguponexperience 

   - SN PostPhDExperience Fellowship 

PostPhDexperience<l year Rs.60,000/PostPhDexperience≥1yearbut<2years Rs.65,000/PostPhDexperience≥2years Rs.70.000/- 

- 8.2.A contingency grant of Rs.30,o00/-per annum towards purchasing consumables, attending conferences, meeting publication charges, etc., will be made available to the fellow on the mentor's recommendation. Any unused amount will be carried forward to the next year.

- 8.3. Institute accommodation shall be provided against a license fee and other due charges as per institute norms subject to availability. As per GOI norms, HRA will be provided if accommodationisunavailable. 

- 8.4.The IPDF will not be eligible to receive any other fellowship from government/nongovernmental sources during the period of their engagement. 

- 8.5. If the candidate resigns from the postdoctoral fellowship before the expiry of the term, the candidate will have to give either one month's notice or deposit one month's fellowship to the Institute for the same. 

- 8.6. Leave rules will be followed as per PhD rules and regulations of the Institute. 

###### 8.7. IPDF is not a regular position of the institution 

- 9.ExternalFundingbasedPost-Doctoral Fellowship(EFPDF)program

###### 8.7. IPDF is not a regular position of the institution 

- 9.ExternalFundingbasedPost-Doctoral Fellowship(EFPDF)program 

EFPDF is admitted to the Post-Doctoral Program of ABV-IIITM, Gwalior, through the procedures adopted by the Institute and avails Fellowships from any recognized funding agencies like ANRF, CSIR, DST, etc. For EFPDF, guidelines of the sponsoring agency will be applicable. 

###### 10.Power to Modify 

Chairperson, Senate is empowered to make any change(s)/Amendment(s)/Exception(s) in the regulations ofthePost-Doctoral Fellowship(PDF)programfrom time to time,

Item 59.0
Opening Remarks by the Chairperson BoG
Chairperson BoG, Prof SN Singh welcomed the members of the Board. He informed the members
that the 5th convocation 2024 which is going to held today is first in NITs/IIITs for passing out
batch 2024. First time, new convention center of the Institute is going to be used for the
convocation. Many construction activities are going on. Prof Anurag Srivastava is attending this
meeting as new senate nominee to the BoG.
Item 59.1
Confirmation of minutes of 58th (02/2024) BoG meeting held on 03.06.2024
The minutes of the meeting of 58th (02/2024) BoG meeting held on 03.06.2024 at ABV-IIITM
Gwalior were circulated to the members and the comments received were incorporated at
appropriate agenda items. So, the minutes of the meeting of 5gth (02/2024) BoG meeting held on
03.06.2024 are confirmed as recirculated.

Item 59.2
Action Taken Report of 58th (02/2024) BoG Meeting
The BoG noted the Action Taken Report (ATR) of the 58th (02/2024) BoG meeting held on
03.06.2024 and expressed satisfaction for works being done at the institute.
BoG suggested that the inclusion of the link between Music and Vedic Mathematics area in the
Indian Knowledge System (IKS) Center be explored. It was also desired by the BoG that the report
of the committee constituted for the survey on lateral/early exit option of the students of IMT
Program be place in next BoG meeting for the information of the BoG.
Item 59.3
ReportbyDirectoroftheInstitute
Director Prof S N Singh informed the BoG about the new activities and events which happened in
the institute after the 58th (02/2024) BoG meeting. Some of them are:
First and second phases of MBA admission is completed, and 50 candidates are admitted
compared to 28 in 2023-24. Institute will go for one spot round during last week of July 2024.

compared to 28 in 2023-24. Institute will go for one spot round during last week of July 2024.
PhD admissions (first and second phases) are completed. Visvesvaraya PhD scheme of MEITY
for 5 seats is also completed. Spot round for PhD (Engineering) will be completed on 21st July
2024.
Counselling of CCMT (for MTech) and JoSSA/CSAB (for BTech and IPG) has started.
Response is good this year in terms of opening and closing ranks in JEE-Mains. MTech
admission seems better this year. Institute will go for filling the vacant MTech seats in August
2024.
Results of all the branches for all the years are declared.
Two big projects (SPARC) of 80+ lakh each have been sanctioned by DST to the institute.
The selection process of rolling advertisement for faculty members at Level -11 and Level 12
is done during June 19-20, 2024 and will be put in this meeting for approval. A fresh
advertisement for all the levels of faculty positions is already issued.

advertisement for all the levels of faculty positions is already issued.
Seven summer courses for backlog students are started. Eighty course backlog students are
taking different courses.
Environmental Day on 5th June 2024 and 10th International Yoga Day on 21st June 2024 were
celebrated in the campus.
The BoG noted the same and expressed happiness on the progress of the institute.

## **<u>Advertisement for the JRF/Project Associate Position in the ANRF Sponsored Project</u>** 

Applications are invited from eligible candidates as a Junior Research Fellow (JRF) or Project Associate-1 to work on the following project sponsored by ANRF under the supervision of Dr. Rahul Kala, **ABV-IIITM, Gwalior** . There is only one position available. The selections would be made for the JRF position. If no candidate is found suitable for the JRF position, candidates for the Project Associate position would be considered. The duration of the position extends for a maximum of three years, extendable upto five years, or the duration of the project, whichever is earlier. The candidates can be enrolled in the Ph.D. program as per the institute norms. The project is being done in collaboration with NIT Mizoram. The details related to the project are as follows:

|**Project No. and Title**|ANRF/ARG/2025/009728/ENS Socially-Interactive Vacuum Cleaning Robot for On-Human Demand and Human-
Instructed Cleaning| |---|---|

metadata.section: Advertisement for the JRF/Project Associate Position in the ANRF Sponsored Project

text:
|---|---| |**About the Project**|Robotic vacuum cleaners are on a steep rise in India. The Indian market has two unique problems that pose a severe
limitation: Target cleaning of room segments, certain surfaces, and only some dirty areas to be cleaned on demand;
and perceiving humans, anticipating their motion, guessing their intents and behaviours, and thus take a path that is
socially compliant during daytime cleaning. The project aims to design a system that allows a human to call the robot;
allow the human to instruct the robot about the cleaning task via speech and hand gestures; perform a semantic
understanding of the robot map and the current perception; make the robot socially compliant with humans; allow
following the person for segments of the journey, enabling the human to point to the area or allowing the human to
inspect the cleaning and give further instructions if needed.| |**Principal Investigator (PI)**|Dr. Rahul Kala|
